items.body: - Pi reads source and capability catalog; proposes patch; validates against pinned artifact; executes comparison with real native evidence; reports gains/confounders. - No automatic live implementation replacement.

items.body: - Remote host authentication, reattachment, native immutable deployment refs, crash/uncertain-operation conformance. - Pi exits without stopping execution. Furnace remains durable authority only when Furnace host chosen.

requirements.text: Pi remains the interactive command/tool/TUI host; a script workflow can be initiated from Pi.
Workflow agent() runs by @anthropic-ai/claude-agent-sdk; trace proves SDK messages and session identity; never silently uses Pi sessions.
Legacy script globals and meta parsing remain supported; baseline golden scripts execute without edits.
Existing non-workflow Pi agent features are not deleted merely to migrate workflow agent().
Host-side node(id,input) is additive and executes without an LLM call for deterministic SDK nodes.
node() input/output enforce JSON transport boundary; malformed/non-serializable payloads fail before provider effects where possible.
Missing provider, unknown capability ID, schema mismatch and unavailable binding fail explicitly, not as null success.
Capability discoverability and capability invocation authorization are independent.
Claude session IDs, input/output, tool events, native SDK failure and token usage are translated without invented values.
Stopping the parent propagates cancellation only through established ownership and appropriate SDK API; stopping observation does not.
The existing workflow tool remains available in Pi without collision or competing shadow tool names.
Old workflow tests remain green under supported upstream mode and new executor-mode tests are added.
At least one real SDK node is proven end-to-end, plus explicit negative controls.
Workflow invocation carries definition, immutable implementation basis and logical invocation ID; native refs remain intact.
Workbench cannot turn absent/unknown/partial producer evidence into successful domain verdict.
Existing Pi inline workflow card and inspector remain operational through migration.
Operator can view node type, name, native ID, current observation freshness, and last error in a terminal detail view.
Pi can query bounded semantic observations without consuming raw event logs or terminal-rendered text.
Forge controls build/test/release verification; no GitHub CI added; no Library dependency.
Upstream MIT license and original copyright retained.
Claude SDK resume reattaches to correct session; invalid or lost session yields explicit failure, never fresh-context masquerading as resume.
Sandbox worker and privileged providers communicate only via validated RPC; hostile scripts cannot acquire host SDK credentials through intended API.
Provider nodes expose inspect/observe only where producer supports them, including event cursor or snapshot freshness.
Pi attaches to an externally started Furnace Run with no causal assumption that Pi owns it.
Workbench distinguishes Run/Work/Attempt, Forge operation and workspace basis, Claude session, HX coverage, RF provenance.
Interrupted effectful operation is reconciled through producer or marked uncertain; no automatic blind repeat.
Terminal inspector supports overview, tree/graph, timeline, detail and a keyboard-only navigation path.
Terminal inspector has plain ASCII tier, theme-aware color tier, and usable 80-column/24-row fallback.
Over 1000 nodes: render cost scales with visible slice and changed ancestors; no full historical-log fold per frame.
Layout, reducers, status classification and control capabilities are pure/testable without a real terminal.
Running and settled Claude conversations can be opened from inspector through Claude transcript adapter.
Pi can use observer tools to inspect definition, retrieve bounded event windows, source/evidence refs and compare two runs.
Hosted MechanicalWorkflows develop() executes actual exported function with explicitly bound native dependencies; fixture outputs cannot be presented as live.
Claude agent receives only curated, authorized provider tool surfaces; list/inspect never grant invoke.
Node events show result/effect distinction (transport, domain and authority-specific status).
Event ingestion can reconnect/deduplicate; gaps and stale timestamps are visible.
Source-defined edges, observed edges and inferred links are distinguishable.
Versioned plan/execute/observe comparison uses immutable source and config digest references.
No automatic code-edit and live replacement of already pinned running execution.
Control actions have native preconditions, permission checks, prompts/confirmations and acknowledgements.
Optional detached workbench host permits Pi client disconnect/reconnect, without falsely claiming crash durability.

Optional Furnace host uses the verified per-Attempt extension-driver semantics (one kept host session per Run's sequential Attempts, each Attempt identified by its admission receipt; work_failure and resident-host indeterminate terminals park the Run for the operator ladder and are never auto-retrie
Optional HX-based cross-product provenance queries, without mandating HX as event store.
RCP-assisted continuation only where explicitly supported and conformance-tested.
Hierarchical agent-swarm aggregation and profile comparisons handle 10k+ nodes subject to benchmarked limits.
Native capability-provider additions require no changes to interpreter core.
Workflow designer can generate tests, source diffs and evidence-linked performance recommendations.
Artifact/host compatibility detects mismatched digest and rejects or explicitly migrates.
Workbench release supports reproducible install and bounded per-provider optional dependencies.
Agent-driven workflow optimization demonstrates measurable improvement without introducing unverified claims.
